subject: SLO remediation request — Palo Foods incident + concession ask
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@palofoods.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@palofoods.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency incident 2026-09-29 — SLO impact and concession request

Team,

We experienced elevated tail latency on our primary inference route during the 09/29 01:00–02:45 UTC window which materially impacted our checkout flow. Our telemetry shows 95th/99th p99 spikes that caused request timeouts and retried client calls. This directly triggered the latency commitment in Section 3.2 of our SOW.

We need the following from Redwood to resolve for leadership and procurement:
- An accounting of the incident window and contributing root causes (we've attached a short log excerpt).
- Confirmation of SLO breach and the mechanism you will use to calculate remediation.
- Proposal for concession: Palo Foods requests a one-month service credit (to apply to our next billing period) in addition to a prorated usage credit for the impacted hours.

Please escalate this to execs for approval — procurement will require formal language and an approved concession form for our renewal. We're on a tight timeline; our CFO is asking for confirmation before 10/05.

Thanks,
Carlos Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure, Palo Foods
Carlos Ruiz

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency incident 2026-09-29 — SLO impact and concession request

Team — forwarding Palo's ask. Summary and proposed approach below.

Summary:
- Incident: 2026-09-29 01:00–02:45 UTC, p99 latency exceeded contractual guardrail on the /generate route for the Redwood-hosted model (customer pinned to rwd-large-v1).
- Impact: customer-visible retries, several failed checkouts; Palo reports measurable revenue impact during the window.
- Customer ask: 1 month service credit + prorated usage credit for impacted hours; needs signed concession language before 2026-10-05.

Our quick analysis (Ops):
- Root cause: transient autoscaler oversubscription during an unexpected regional spike; a fallback routing misconfiguration caused requests to hit a higher-latency model variant during the load spike.
- Remediation already applied: routing policy tightened, autoscaler limits increased, and a post-incident KV-cache warmup tweak rolled out.

Proposed concession (recommended):
- Technical remediation report to Palo (1–page summary, Ops + SRE).
- Offer: one month free of service (applied as an account-level credit) OR 10% usage credit for the next invoice plus a $10k one-time service credit. Recommend selecting the option that aligns to finance guidance.
- Non-precedent clause: attach a short concession form that marks this as a one-off (legal to draft).

As this exceeds the delegated credit bands, please approve at exec level: 1) one month free OR 2) 10% usage credit + $10k credit. If approved, we'll prepare the concession form and route to Legal + Finance for sign-off and send to Palo with HubSpot ticket HS-32489.

I'll include the Ops incident timeline and the Palo excerpt in the follow-up.

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Account Strategy, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency incident 2026-09-29 — Exec decision and approved concession

Thanks for the clear analysis, Karthik. I reviewed Ops notes and Palo's impact summary. Approve a constrained concession with the following terms: 

Approved concession (executive sign-off):
- Offer Palo Foods a single account credit equal to one month of standard subscription fees capped at $25,000 OR a blended alternative: 10% usage credit for the next invoice plus a one-time $7,500 service credit. (Customer may choose which option.)
- Require Legal to include a one-off "no-precedent" clause and standard indemnity/limitation language; Marketing and Sales may not publicly reference this concession.
- Condition acceptance on customer acknowledging the remediation steps and agreeing to a short post-mortem meeting with our SRE team within 10 business days.
- Finance to prepare the credit memo and post the adjustment against HS-32489; include a short amortization note if the customer chooses the usage-credit path.

Please prepare the concession form (use template: approved_concession_form.pdf) and route to Palo with the HubSpot ticket link. Once Legal stamps it, proceed to finalize and obtain customer sign-off.

One operational ask: capture explicit telemetry windows and the hour-by-hour calculation we will use to compute the prorated usage credit so there is no ambiguity. Ops, please include the calculation spreadsheet as an attachment in the HubSpot ticket.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
